cycles.method: No chip-cycle bound or worst-case interrupt timing for 0.3.1 or 0.3.2 (0.3.2 changes only how the card build's machine chooser draws its rows; the render and its limits are 0.3.1's). Instead the module bounds its own time: pm_govern (pool.c) reads the frame timer around each POLY render and sheds voices above 40 % of a frame on average or 26,000 counts (about 197 us) in one frame. evidence/performance-t06.json records historical native instruction averages only. The owner waived chip worst-case cycles for this exact source (sdk/poly8-build-approval.json).

load.method: No cfmeter.py capture for 0.3.1 or 0.3.2. Measured for 0.3.1 with the frame timer on the owner's MKII, RAM-booted development twin of the beta base without cached module code (23 Oct 2026): POLY render share 8.7/25.3/34.2/40.8 % of the CPU for 1-4 held voices; with eight keys held and the limit active the longest frame's POLY time was 24,781 counts (188 us) and the panel kept answering. 0.3.0 on the same twin reached 100 % CPU at three to four voices and froze the panel for about 33 s.

stress.droppedExplanation: No qualified wire-rate MIDI flood for 0.3.1 or 0.3.2. Panel stress, 0.3.1 on the owner's MKII twin: eight held keys, chords over the playing sequencer and 40 rapid presses with a six-key chord; no freeze, no stall record, longest masked span in the key handlers 1,937 counts (15 us).

nativeEvidence.method: Historical 0.2.5/T06 only: twelve 1,000-block before/after native ColdFire instruction comparisons; all eight-channel 16,000-frame audio comparisons identical. They do not qualify 0.3.1. For 0.3.1, USB recordings of the same pattern from PLAY match 0.3.0 to the recorder floor (residual RMS 5e-8 against a 7.5e-4 signal) on cached and uncached twins.
